### policy_conflict_scan

Scope of the structured policy: the base section of `controls.extended.yaml` is byte-for-byte the blueprint charter (`products/controls.yaml` is a prefix of the extended file; every top-level key compares equal after YAML load), plus five `extended_policies`, each with `overwrite: []`:

| id | trigger | subject | computes | target_tool (owner) | prerequisite |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| controls_ext_support_overage_charge | state_due | controls_invoice_charged | charge_amount_usd | charge_controls_support_overage_c0d5009e (agent) | [] |
| controls_ext_arrears_settlement | on_request | controls_payment_received | payment_amount_usd | record_controls_plan_payment_09134fd7 (user) | support_overage_charge (value_input, state) |
| controls_ext_reinstatement_charge | on_request | controls_plan_reinstated | reinstatement_charge_usd | reinstate_controls_plan_58d0efe4 (agent) | arrears_settlement (state_gate, state) |
| controls_ext_alarm_ack_credit | state_due | controls_credit_issued | credit_amount_usd | issue_controls_alarm_credit_7b85e02f (agent) | [] |
| controls_ext_upgrade_authorisation | on_request | controls_invoice_charged | authorised_labor_usd | authorise_controls_upgrade_c5086d5b (user) | alarm_ack_credit (value_input, state) |

Two disjoint trees: T-A = {reinstatement_charge ← arrears_settlement ← support_overage_charge} and T-B = {upgrade_authorisation ← alarm_ack_credit}. The five policies are covered exactly once by the two trees, so the two tasks' scopes (one tree each) are pairwise disjoint and jointly complete over the extended charter — provided task 0 claims T-A and task 1 claims T-B, which the per-task files confirm from their worlds (a suspended plan with arrears / an active plan with unacknowledged alarms and an upgrade request); the masked `charter_scope` fields are compared after the freezes.

Overlapping subjects among the extended policies: `controls_invoice_charged` is the subject of both support_overage_charge (charge_type support_overage) and upgrade_authorisation (charge_type upgrade_labor); the two are separated by charge_type and by tool, and no task world triggers both (T-A's world has no upgrade request; T-B's plan has no uncovered support hours — `support_hours_remaining` 0.5, hours logged 7.5 against a pool of 8.0). No two extended policies gate on the same time anchor with different counting rules. Terminal states: each write is one atomic effect (one event row + one `balance_due` update; reinstatement also flips `status` and stamps `reinstatement_date`; upgrade authorisation also files a `controls_requests` row) — none of the five tools reads or judges any other policy's state (function bodies quoted under `prerequisite_graph`).

Cross-category read boundaries: every `cross_category` entry declares `as: branch` or `as: existence` with the fields read; the computes read only `status`, `remote_monitoring_included`, `repair_labor_discount_pct`, `agreement_labor_rate_usd`, `repair_labor_covered`, `bundle_credit_with_controls_usd` (maintenance) and `status`, `data_source`, `meters_covered`, `subscription_fee_per_meter_usd`, `meters_included` (energy) — all present on those products' holding rows or variant tables (`products/maintenance.yaml`, `products/energy.yaml` variant parameters checked). Declared and exercised reads coincide (gate: "cross-category reads declared exactly").

Conflicts between the extended rules and the base rules on the quantities they score are found and listed under `override_declarations` (F1–F4). They are charter-global facts; their cost to a task is demonstrated in that task's file.

### rule_compute_equivalence

Method: for every binding of every policy, the `compute_basis` quotation was located verbatim in that policy's `rule` (every quotation is one or more rule sentences; the script check that flagged multi-sentence quotations as "not verbatim" only reflects the sentences being non-adjacent in the rule — each sentence is present), and each expression was read against its sentence. Findings by policy:

**controls_ext_support_overage_charge** — windows: `within_months=12, date_field='resolved_date'` = "twelve months to the handling day" ✓; `pool_credited` sums every `controls_support_hours_credited` row with no window = "the support hours the plan has been credited under its entitlement" ✓ (both faces agree; see O-2 for the realism of an unwindowed sum); `remote_rate`, `onsite_visits_absorbed`, `onsite_rate`, `nff_share`, `out_of_hours_rate` ladders each match their three rule sentences tier for tier ✓; `onsite_allowance_hours = visits × 4` ✓ ("each attendance reckoned at four hours"); `pool_applied_to_onsite` fall-through `RND(pool × onsite_after / MX(1, onsite_after + remote), 2)` = "in the proportion each bears to the two of them together" (the `MX(1, …)` guard is a compute-only convention that departs from the proportion only when the two together are below one hour — O-3); `billable_onsite = MX(0, onsite_after − pool_applied)` and `billable_remote = MX(0, remote − MX(0, pool − pool_applied))` implement "the on-site hours left after the visit allowance and the drawing … and the remote hours left after the drawing" ✓; `result` = sum of the four bands, rounded once ✓. **Defect F5**: the first two tiers of the drawdown ladder each end with an exclusive clause — "…drawn first against the on-site hours left after the visit allowance, **and only the remote hours left over are billed**" / "…drawn first against the remote hours, **and only the on-site hours left over are billed**" — while the compute bills the residue of the *other* band whenever the pool is smaller than the band drawn first (`billable_onsite` and `billable_remote` are both computed under every tier). The rule states two things about the same quantity: the general sentence bills both residues, the tier sentence says "only" one band is billed. Both faces cannot be read as one; recorded as SOURCE-POLICY RED (F5), demonstrated in task 0.

**controls_ext_arrears_settlement** — `outstanding_charges = MX(0, charges − payments − credits)` ✓; `due_charges_12m` (within 12 months by `due_date`, which excludes a future due day because `MONTHS` goes negative) = "already fallen due within the twelve months to the handling day" ✓; `recent_due_charges` within 1 month by due_date = "fell due inside the last month" ✓; `charge_lines_12m` counts charge rows by `due_date` while the sentence says "charges **raised** on the plan" in the twelve months — the row has no raised date, so due_date is the only anchor available; the two faces agree in every task world here (O-4); `payments_recent` within 4 months by received_date ✓; `required_charges` ladder ✓; `months_overdue = MX(0, MONTHS(last_plan_fee_due, NOW))` = "whole months … counted from that due day to the handling day" ✓ — but the sentence conditions on the charge having "**stood unpaid** past its due day" and the compute never tests whether that plan-fee charge is paid (O-5; no consequence in either task because the latest plan fee is unpaid in task 0 and task 1 does not run this policy); `late_fee_rate` tiers ✓ (`RND(pct × months / 100, 6)` for ≥3 whole months; `pct/100` "for one month" for 1–2; 0 otherwise, only on quarterly/monthly billing) ✓; `late_fee = required × rate` = "acts on the charges required now and on nothing else" ✓; `instalment_value` = annual fee / instalments per year ✓; `plan_withdrawn = status == suspended and DAYS(suspension_date, NOW) > 0` = "have stood withdrawn since the day recorded on the plan" ✓; `advance_share` ✓; `trueup_months` (3 for quarterly/monthly true-up; `MONTHS(NOW, term_end_date)` for annual/semiannual) ✓; `point_overage_due = excess × fee × months / 12` ✓; `shared_licence_allowance` (`fee_per_meter × meters / 12`, halved for `mixed`) ✓, read from the owner's first active energy subscription at any site — the rule says "an energy monitoring subscription the owner holds", so both faces agree (O-6 on the base being site-scoped); `settlement_discount_pct` ✓; `gross_due`, `net_due`, `result` follow the closing sentence's order (late fee on required charges; advance and point overage added; allowance off before the discount; discount once; one rounding) ✓.

**controls_ext_reinstatement_charge** — `withdrawal_span_days = DAYS(suspension_date, NOW)` = "that day excluded and the handling day included" ✓; `base_fee` ladder ✓ (> 60 days and points above / at-or-below the covered maximum); `gateway_fee` ladder ✓ (> 30 days; full / half / quarter); `withdrawn_days` ladder ✓ (24/7 desk and `reinstatement_date` non-empty → from that day; extended/business hours and ≥ 3 charge lines in 12 months → from the latest plan-fee due day; otherwise from the suspension day); `months_withdrawn = int(days / 30)` = "thirty days to the month and dropping any part month" ✓; `resync_monthly_fee` ✓; `backfill_fee` ✓ (0.1 h × meters × technician rate, halved for `mixed`); `survey_share` ✓ (> restart window and no / ≥ 1 software update in 12 months); `result` = plain sum, one rounding ✓.

**controls_ext_alarm_ack_credit** — `unacked_critical` / `unacked_urgent` count `controls_alarm_raised` rows within 12 months by `raised_timestamp` with `acknowledged_timestamp=''` = "the records show with no acknowledgement" ✓; `credited_alarms` ladder ✓ (`int(urgent/2)` = "taken down to a whole alarm"); `critical_raised` counts every critical alarm, acknowledged or not = "three or more alarms classed as critical" ✓; `credit_unit` ✓; `bundled_uplift = bundle_credit / alarm_responses_included_per_year` (halved) = "that agreement's own annual credit for holding an automation plan, taken over the plan year's included alarm responses" ✓; `repeat_step_pct` ✓ (`alarms_raised` counts every raised alarm of any class = "monitored alarms raised in all" ✓); `data_gap_credit` ✓; `result = credited × (unit + uplift) × (1 + step) + data_gap` = the closing sentence ✓.

**controls_ext_upgrade_authorisation** — `head_end_hours` ladder ✓ (`panels_covered >= panels_covered_max`); `point_blocks = int(points / 100)` = "each whole hundred points" ✓; `upgrade_hours` ladder ✓ (`controller_generation >= min_controller_generation + 4` = "a generation at least four years newer than the oldest the tier supports"); `technician_rate` ladder ✓; `discount_pct` ladder ✓ (+15 / +7 points); `quoted_labor = hours × rate × (1 − discount)` ✓ "acts on the priced hours once"; `migration_allowance` ✓ (quarter / eighth hour per meter at the tier's technician rate when the subscription reads the controls system and covers more / no more meters than its tier includes); `standing_credit` = all credits ever issued ✓ "the credit standing on the plan"; `charges_12m` by due_date and `payments_12m` by received_date ✓; `credit_offset` ✓; `result = MX(0, quoted − migration − offset)` rounded once ✓.

Sweep back (rule → compute): no rule sentence of any policy is without an implementing binding, and no binding rests on a basis the rule does not state, other than the two conventions noted (`MX(1, …)` guard, O-3; the unpaid test missing from `months_overdue`, O-5) and the exclusive "only … are billed" clauses of F5.

### action_binding_and_uuids

- `(target_tool, computes)` pairs: five distinct pairs, each claimed by exactly one policy (script check: no duplicate claims).
- uuid8 tails: `c0d5009e`, `09134fd7`, `58d0efe4`, `7b85e02f`, `c5086d5b` — all eight lowercase hex characters, pairwise distinct, no shared prefix, no sequential or adjacent values, no tail that looks copied and re-suffixed. Each is frozen with its tool in `task_tools.py`.
- Docstrings: none of the five names another tool, states a position in a sequence, or carries "before/after/first". `record_controls_plan_payment_09134fd7` and `authorise_controls_upgrade_c5086d5b` are `owner="user"`; the other three `owner="agent"`.
- Business reading of each binding: charge_controls_support_overage → one `controls_invoice_charged` row `charge_type=support_overage`, balance up ✓ matches the policy; record_controls_plan_payment → one `controls_payment_received` row, balance down ✓; reinstate_controls_plan → status active, `reinstatement_date` = today, one `controls_invoice_charged` row `charge_type=reinstatement`, balance up ✓; authorise_controls_upgrade → one `controls_requests` row `request_type=upgrade_authorization, outcome=confirmed` plus one `controls_invoice_charged` row `charge_type=upgrade_labor`, balance up ✓. **Defect F6**: `issue_controls_alarm_credit_7b85e02f` admits a second business reading. Its docstring says "Put a credit back … for monitored alarm responses the owner should never have been billed for … for alarm work wrongly counted past the plan year's included responses", and its body hard-codes `credit_reason="nuisance_alarm_overage"`, while the policy it serves (controls_ext_alarm_ack_credit, base ref "Credits for a missed acknowledgement target are applied to the next plan invoice") credits alarms the desk never acknowledged, and the schema carries the value `missed_acknowledgement` in the `credit_reason` enum (`db_schema.json` → controls_events.credit_reason: `["missed_acknowledgement", "nuisance_alarm_overage", "billing_adjustment", "goodwill"]`). The tool's stated purpose and the policy's purpose are different business events; the row it leaves is stamped with the wrong reason. Recorded as SOURCE-POLICY RED (F6), demonstrated in task 1.
- Tool-side additions: `charge_controls_support_overage_c0d5009e` writes no `due_date` on the charge row, although the base billing rule says every invoice falls due the tier's payment term after the invoice date; the arrears policy's "already fallen due" reads `due_date` and so can never see that charge as due (O-7; no consequence in task 0 because the tier taken requires every unsettled charge). `record_controls_plan_payment_09134fd7` writes no `invoice_ref`, so the base sentence "Payments are applied to the oldest unpaid invoice unless the owner names one" has nothing to bind to (O-8).

### prerequisite_sentences

E1 — arrears_settlement waits on support_overage_charge. Sentence (arrears rule, sentence 2): "The sum required to settle a plan is fixed only after every hour of controls support work the plan's included support hours do not cover stands invoiced on the plan's billing history." Four-point test: (1) joins this policy's own result ("the sum required to settle") to what it waits on with "only after" ✓; (2) state form: "stands invoiced on the plan's billing history" is a record-visible state in the words the finder uses (`find_controls_events`: "the plan's invoices, payments and credits") with no performer, no action, no tool ✓; (3) no tool name, policy id, snake_case token or row id ✓; (4) strength: the edge `condition` ("The plan's billing history carries an invoiced charge for the support hours logged against resolved tickets beyond the included support hours standing to the plan's credit") is the same state at the same scope (one open-ended class, "every hour … not covered", stated open) ✓. One write brings the state about: the only tool creating a `controls_invoice_charged` row of `charge_type=support_overage` is `charge_controls_support_overage_c0d5009e`; the other two charge-creating tools write `reinstatement` and `upgrade_labor`. Derivation for a reader: sentence → "hours the included support hours do not cover" → the only rule whose subject is "Controls support work that a plan's included support hours do not cover is invoiced … as a support overage" is support_overage_charge → its target tool. One reading. The arrears rule carries no second wording of this dependency; the overage rule does not restate it.

E2 — reinstatement_charge waits on arrears_settlement. Sentence (reinstatement rule, sentence 2): "Remote access and alarm monitoring are restored and the reinstatement charge raised only once the balance owed under the plan stands at nil or below." (1) "only once" joins this policy's result (restoration + charge) to the state ✓; (2) "the balance owed under the plan" is `controls_plans.balance_due` in the finder's words (`find_controls_plans`: "the balance owed"), no action, no performer ✓; (3) no tool/id/token ✓; (4) `condition` "The balance owed under the automation service plan is nil or below at the moment the plan is put back into service" is the same threshold ✓. Which write brings the state about: the arrears rule opens "A building owner who wants an automation service plan put back in order settles it in one payment" — the payment tool lowers `balance_due` by the paid sum. Structurally a second tool, `issue_controls_alarm_credit_7b85e02f`, also lowers `balance_due`; but its policy fixes the credit at the count of unacknowledged critical/urgent alarms times a unit, never at the balance, so it cannot be read as the write that brings "nil or below" about, and in T-A's world there are no alarm rows at all. Recorded as observation O-9 (structural), not RED: the hop resolves in one reading. The reinstatement rule carries nothing else about the dependency; the arrears rule does not restate it.

E3 — upgrade_authorisation waits on alarm_ack_credit. Sentence (upgrade rule, sentence 2): "The labor the owner is asked to authorise is fixed only after every monitored alarm the records show with no acknowledgement carries its credit on the plan's balance." (1) "only after" ✓; (2) "carries its credit on the plan's balance" is a record-visible state (a credit row on the plan's history / the balance) with no performer ✓; (3) no tool/id/token ✓; (4) `condition` "The plan's balance carries a credit entry for the monitored alarms the records show with no acknowledgement" — same state, same scope ✓. One write: the only credit-creating tool is `issue_controls_alarm_credit_7b85e02f`, and the only rule whose subject is credit for "A monitored alarm the desk never acknowledged" is alarm_ack_credit ✓. One reading. No second wording; not restated in the credit rule.

Cross-problem orders stated by any rule that ground no declared edge: none found in the five extended rules. Base rule sentences stating a cross-problem order that a tree rests on: the base sentence "Access and monitoring are restored when the arrears are settled in full and the tier's reinstatement fee is charged" (controls_suspension_and_reinstatement) states the same order as E2, but E2 rests on the extended rule's own sentence, so the base sentence is background, not the ground of the edge (observation O-10, no defect).

State-form priority: all three edges are state-form; nothing to test under fallback.

### override_declarations

All five policies declare `overwrite: []`. The base section is verbatim. Sentence-by-sentence conclusions against each `base_policy_refs` entry, plus the base policies that govern the same quantities without being cited:

**controls_ext_support_overage_charge** (refs: controls_billing_and_late_fee, controls_portfolio_interaction).
- billing_and_late_fee: "Extra services — support hours beyond the pool, … — are invoiced in the month they are performed rather than held to the year end." — the extended policy invoices the uncovered hours of a trailing twelve-month window in one charge at handling; the base sentence has them invoiced month by month. Same quantity (the support overage), different handling; undeclared. Other sentences of that base policy (instalment invoicing, due day counting, late fee, credits, payment application) are not touched by this policy ✓ inherited.
- portfolio_interaction: "A controls fault found during a maintenance visit is logged as a ticket on this plan and drawn from its support pool, not billed as maintenance work" — followed (tickets are read from the plan's own history) ✓; the energy and project sentences do not bear on this quantity ✓.
- **Uncited but governing: controls_support_handling** — "The hours logged against a resolved ticket are drawn from the plan year's support pool, and once the pool is exhausted further hours are billed at the tier's support hour rate, with on-site hours billed at the controls technician rate instead." and its formula `overage_charge_usd = round(max(0, support_hours - support_hour_pool) * support_hour_rate_usd, 2)`, with measure `controls_msr_support_hours_used_year` over the **plan year**. The extended rule (a) takes a twelve-month window instead of the plan year, (b) deducts four hours per included on-site visit before any drawing, (c) has hours closed with no fault found "never draw the included support hours", (d) bills remote hours at the support hour rate **less six or twelve per cent** and on-site hours at **the maintenance agreement's labor rate or the technician rate less eight per cent**, and (e) adds an out-of-hours uplift. Each of (a)–(e) handles the quantity the base sentence fixes differently, and none is named in `overwrite`. **F1: undeclared override, SOURCE-POLICY RED**; consequence (two defensible overage figures) demonstrated in task 0.

**controls_ext_arrears_settlement** (refs: controls_billing_and_late_fee).
- "an invoice unpaid past its due day carries the tier's late fee for each month or part month it stays unpaid" and formula `late_fee_usd = round(amount_usd * late_fee_pct_per_month / 100, 2)` (per invoice, per month or part month, at every tier) — the extended rule's baseline is "No late fee is added to the charges required now", and its ladder charges the rate only on quarterly/monthly plans, on "the charges required now" rather than on each overdue invoice, for **whole** months only, and for a flat one month when the arrears have run one or two whole months. Same quantity (what the owner must pay), different rule; undeclared. **F2: SOURCE-POLICY RED**; consequence demonstrated in task 0.
- "Payments are applied to the oldest unpaid invoice unless the owner names one" — the payment tool records no invoice; observation O-8.
- "Each invoice falls due the tier's payment term after the invoice date…" — inherited, not touched ✓. Instalment invoicing and credits sentences — not touched ✓.
- Uncited but read: controls_agg_portfolio_point_pricing "Points beyond a plan's covered maximum are charged the tier's point overage fee for the remainder of the plan year, prorated by whole months" — the extended tier for annual/semiannual true-up ("every whole month left in the plan term") gives the same figure; the quarterly/monthly tier ("the three months to the next true-up") differs from "the remainder of the plan year" — undeclared, no consequence in either task (task 0's tier is annual). Observation O-11.

**controls_ext_reinstatement_charge** (refs: controls_suspension_and_reinstatement).
- "Access and monitoring are restored when the arrears are settled in full and the tier's reinstatement fee is charged" — the extended baseline already charges more than the tier's reinstatement fee (a quarter of the gateway fee is added in the baseline itself), and the ladder raises the fee by twenty or forty per cent and adds gateway, re-synchronisation, back-fill and survey elements. Same quantity (the charge raised at reinstatement), different value; undeclared. **F3: SOURCE-POLICY RED**; consequence demonstrated in task 0.
- "the support pool and alarm allowance are not topped up on reinstatement" — followed (the tool touches neither) ✓.
- "A plan that lapsed at its term end may be restarted without a fresh site survey only inside the tier's restart window …; past that the system is surveyed again before any plan is quoted" — this governs expired plans; the extended rule applies the restart window to a **suspended** plan and takes a share of the survey fee instead of requiring a survey — a different subject, so not a conflict on the same situation; observation O-12.
- Suspension sentence (when access is withdrawn) — not touched ✓.

**controls_ext_alarm_ack_credit** (refs: controls_billing_and_late_fee).
- "Credits for a missed acknowledgement target are applied to the next plan invoice." — the base fixes where the credit lands, not its amount; the extended fixes the amount. The tool reduces `balance_due` immediately rather than applying to the next plan invoice — a timing difference, not a scored-quantity conflict; observation O-13.
- Uncited but governing: controls_alarm_monitoring "A critical or urgent alarm is acknowledged inside the tier's acknowledgement target, counted in elapsed minutes from the moment the alarm was raised" — the base's "missed acknowledgement target" includes an alarm acknowledged **late**; the extended credits only alarms "with no acknowledgement" at all. Different handling; undeclared. No consequence in task 1 (the only acknowledged critical alarm, AL-10005130, was acknowledged 29 minutes after being raised, inside the Alarm Monitoring Plan's 60-minute target), so recorded as observation O-14 rather than RED.
- Uncited: controls_activation_and_entitlement "Where the tier includes no alarm monitoring, no alarm allowance is credited and alarms from that site reach nobody" — the ladder tier "the tier watches alarms only during its own monitoring hours" can only be met by the Controls Help Desk Subscription (`alarm_monitoring_hours: business_hours`), the one tier with `alarm_monitoring_included: false`, whose alarms the base says reach nobody and whose compensation demands the blueprint routes to POLICY_NOT_COVERED. That tier is therefore either vacuous or in conflict with base; observation O-1.

**controls_ext_upgrade_authorisation** (refs: controls_billing_and_late_fee, controls_portfolio_interaction).

### factor_ladders

Per policy (effect label; `decides`; tiers; multi-source; distinct outcomes; label honesty; cross-difficulty). Every ladder has exactly three tiers, the fall-through counted; every non-fall-through tier is stated in the rule verbatim (script containment ✓) and implemented as the matching branch of the `decides` binding; every factor's `decides` is a compute binding other than `result`; binding sets are disjoint within each policy; each factor's fall-through is its `baseline`.

**support_overage_charge** — 6 factors: 5 parameter, 1 method.
- pool_drawdown_order (method; pool_applied_to_onsite): tiers = [escalation ∧ maintenance active → draw on-site first; escalation ∧ no maintenance active → draw remote first; otherwise → proportional]; multi-source (tier param ∧ maintenance holding) ✓; three distinct algorithms ✓ method honest; cross_difficulty maintenance ✓. Realism: a bundled maintenance customer having the pool absorb on-site time first is what a contractor with a maintenance bundle does ✓; the fall-through proportional draw is a published default ✓.
- support_hour_volume_rate (parameter; remote_rate): [hours ≥ 3×pool ∧ ≥ 3 on-site tickets → rate −12%; 2×pool ≤ hours < 3×pool ∧ ≥ 1 on-site ticket → rate −6%; otherwise → tier rate]; multi-source (hours sum ∧ credited sum ∧ on-site ticket count, distinct rows) ✓; distinct values ✓; volume discount is a thing that line weighs ✓.
- onsite_labor_rate (parameter; onsite_rate): [maintenance active ∧ repair discount ≥ 10% → agreement labor rate; active ∧ < 10% → technician rate −8%; otherwise → technician rate]; multi-source (status ∧ tier param of the other product) ✓; cross_difficulty maintenance ✓; distinct ✓.
- no_fault_hours_share (parameter; nff_share): [remote fix included ∧ ≥ 2 NFF tickets → 0; remote fix ∧ exactly 1 → ½; otherwise → 1]; multi-source ✓; distinct ✓. Realism: waiving no-fault-found hours where the tier includes a remote fix attempt is a defensible published treatment (the desk eats its own fruitless remote investigations); that the waiver grows with the count is odd but not something the business would not publish — kept, noted as O-15.
- onsite_visit_allowance (parameter; onsite_visits_absorbed): [maintenance active ∧ remote monitoring included → +2 visits; active ∧ not included → +1; otherwise → tier's visits]; multi-source ✓; cross_difficulty maintenance ✓; distinct ✓.
- out_of_hours_uplift (parameter; out_of_hours_rate): [business-hours desk ∧ ≥ 1 monitoring-desk ticket → ½ rate/hour; extended-hours desk ∧ ≥ 1 → ¼ rate/hour; otherwise → 0]; multi-source ✓; distinct ✓; every tier reachable (business_hours: Help Desk, Alarm Monitoring; extended: Scheduled, Software Assurance; 24/7: the two top tiers).
Counts: parameter 5 / method 1 / multi-source 6 / cross_difficulty 3 (maintenance).

**arrears_settlement** — 6 factors: 5 parameter, 1 method.
- charges_required_now (method; required_charges): [≥ 3 charge lines in 12 m ∧ no payment in 4 m → everything unsettled; ≥ 3 ∧ a payment in 4 m → unsettled less last month's due; otherwise → only what has fallen due in 12 m less paid/credited]; multi-source (charge rows ∧ payment rows) ✓; three distinct algorithms ✓; cross_difficulty null.
- arrears_late_fee_rate (parameter; late_fee_rate): [≥ 3 whole months ∧ quarterly/monthly billing → pct × months; 1–2 months ∧ quarterly/monthly → pct × 1; otherwise → 0]; multi-source (latest due date ∧ tier param) ✓; distinct ✓.
- advance_instalment_share (parameter; advance_share): [withdrawn ∧ required ≥ 2 instalments → 1; withdrawn ∧ 1 ≤ required < 2 → ½; otherwise → 0]; multi-source (plan status/date ∧ computed charges) ✓; distinct ✓.
- point_overage_months_up_front (parameter; trueup_months): [points > max ∧ quarterly/monthly true-up → 3; points > max ∧ annual/semiannual → whole months left in term; otherwise → 0]; multi-source (plan field ∧ tier param ∧ term end) ✓; distinct ✓.
- shared_point_licence_allowance (parameter; shared_licence_allowance): [energy active ∧ controls_system → fee/meter/12 × meters; active ∧ mixed → half; otherwise → 0]; multi-source ✓; cross_difficulty energy ✓; distinct ✓.

### findings

Charter-global findings (each names the task whose file demonstrates the consequence):

- **F1 — SOURCE-POLICY RED (undeclared override, support overage).** Symptom: two rules fix the support overage. Root cause: `controls_ext_support_overage_charge` re-derives the quantity that base `controls_support_handling` fixes (plan-year pool draw at the support hour / technician rate, formula `overage_charge_usd`) with a different window, a visit allowance, a no-fault waiver, discounted rates and an uplift, while `overwrite: []` and the base policy is not even in `base_policy_refs`. Evidence: quoted under override_declarations. Consequence: task 0 (`0.md` § policy_self_consistency) — two defensible overage charges. Location: `controls.extended.yaml` extended_policies[0].overwrite / rule; base policies[controls_support_handling].rule + formula.
- **F2 — SOURCE-POLICY RED (undeclared override, late fee).** Base `controls_billing_and_late_fee` "carries the tier's late fee for each month or part month it stays unpaid" per invoice vs the extended baseline "No late fee is added" and a whole-month, quarterly/monthly-only ladder on "the charges required now". Consequence: task 0 — two defensible settlement sums. Location: extended_policies[1].overwrite / rule.
- **F3 — SOURCE-POLICY RED (undeclared override, reinstatement fee).** Base `controls_suspension_and_reinstatement` "the tier's reinstatement fee is charged" vs the extended baseline's fee + quarter gateway and the ladder's raised fee. Consequence: task 0 — two defensible reinstatement charges. Location: extended_policies[2].overwrite / rule.
- **F4 — SOURCE-POLICY RED (undeclared override, upgrade labor discount).** Base `controls_software_and_security` "quoted, with the tier's upgrade labor discount applied" vs the extended ladder raising the discount by 15/7 points and repricing the hours at the maintenance rate. Consequence: task 1 — two defensible authorised-labor figures. Location: extended_policies[4].overwrite / rule.
- **F5 — SOURCE-POLICY RED (rule/compute equivalence, drawdown tiers).** The two non-fall-through tiers of `pool_drawdown_order` say "only the remote hours left over are billed" / "only the on-site hours left over are billed" while the compute bills the residue of both bands under every tier. Consequence: task 0 — two readings, two numbers. Location: extended_policies[0].rule (the two "Where the tier includes an on-site controls visit escalation…" sentences) vs compute `billable_onsite` / `billable_remote`.
- **F6 — SOURCE-POLICY RED (action binding admits two business readings).** `issue_controls_alarm_credit_7b85e02f`'s docstring describes a credit for "alarm work wrongly counted past the plan year's included responses" and stamps `credit_reason="nuisance_alarm_overage"`; the policy credits missed acknowledgements and the schema has `missed_acknowledgement`. Consequence: task 1. Location: `task_tools.py` lines 139–172.

Observations (no demonstrable consequence on either world; recorded, not grounds for rework):

- O-1 — `alarms_credited_basis` tier 2 ("watches alarms only during its own monitoring hours") is reachable only at the Controls Help Desk Subscription, which watches no alarms; the ladder is effectively two-tiered for every monitored plan.
- O-2 — `pool_credited` sums every `controls_support_hours_credited` row ever, so a plan in its second plan year would carry a doubled "included support hours standing to the plan's credit" although base says hours never carry forward; both faces of the extended rule agree, so no equivalence failure.
- O-3 — the `MX(1, …)` denominator guard in the proportional draw departs from "the proportion each bears" only when on-site-after-allowance plus remote hours are below one hour.
- O-4 — `charge_lines_12m` is windowed by `due_date` while the sentence says "charges raised"; no raised date exists on the row.
- O-5 — `months_overdue` never tests that the latest plan-fee charge is unpaid, although the sentence says "has stood unpaid past its due day".
- O-6 — the energy reads (`CFIELD/CPARAM('energy', status='active')`) are owner-scoped (any site) while base `controls_portfolio_interaction` is site-scoped ("the same controls system"); both extended faces say "the owner holds".
- O-7 — `charge_controls_support_overage_c0d5009e` writes no `due_date`; the arrears "already fallen due" test can never see that charge.
- O-8 — `record_controls_plan_payment_09134fd7` writes no `invoice_ref`; base "applied to the oldest unpaid invoice" has nothing to bind to.
- O-9 — a credit also lowers `balance_due`, so structurally two tools move E2's waited-on state; the credit rule cannot be read as bringing "nil or below" about (its amount is fixed by alarm counts).
- O-10 — base "Access and monitoring are restored when the arrears are settled in full" states E2's order; the edge rests on the extended sentence, so this is background.
- O-11 — the quarterly/monthly point-overage tier ("three months to the next true-up") differs from base "remainder of the plan year"; not exercised by either task.
- O-12 — the survey-fee share applies the restart window to a suspended plan; base's restart window governs expired plans.
- O-13 — the credit and upgrade-labor tools move `balance_due` immediately; base has credits "applied to the next plan invoice" and extra services "invoiced in the month performed" — timing, not amount.
- O-14 — base treats a late acknowledgement as a missed target; extended credits only alarms never acknowledged; not exercised (task 1's acknowledged critical alarm was inside its target).
- O-15 — the no-fault waiver grows with the number of no-fault tickets; defensible as a published treatment, noted for realism.
